62905250
>>62905187
HOA communities are basically neighborhoods where old boomers can tell you what to do on your land and make sure you conform to their rules and desires. Basically, they are places for people who want to live among others who think like they do, aka drone mentality. For example, no vegetable gardens on the front yard, no clothes drying on the yard, no car repairs or old shitbox vehicles in your driveway, no clutter on the balcony, stuff like that. If you cause disturbances to other neighbors you can be forcibly removed.

Now obviously if you live without a hoa you have almost complete freedom subject to compliance with county or city ordinances. I have a very expansive property but there is a neighbor next to me renting a house and hes a nut job that goes on loud rants to himself at night sometimes. Even though I have 3 acres, his voice still echoes up the hill and I can hear him. In any HOA community, he would be quickly removed. But alas, these are the prices we pay for freedom.

Latest replies (last 30, oldest → newest)

62905267
>>62905187
Other countries have HOA's too. Mexico, for example. If you live in a gated community, someone needs to actually maintain the gate. If you have a pool, someone needs to maintain the pool. If you need landscaping, someone needs to pay for that. HOA's are just vehicles to pay for that. Basically every Condo building has an HOA equivalent because you literally have to pay for maintenance and insurance on a 30 story building. In theory, an HOA is the perfect example of what your taxes to the government should do. In practice, they end up very bloated and inefficient, or so cheap that they don't maintain the community anymore. Also the boards are always dominated by little cliques of hotheaded personalities, because no one else wants to be an HOA janny and do it for free.

I learned my lesson and won't be living in one again.
